definitions.explanation: Describes something complicated or requiring effort that one would rather avoid.

examples.japanese: {手続|てつづ}きが{煩|わずら}わしくて{嫌|いや}になる。
examples.english: The procedures are so troublesome that I'm fed up.

examples.japanese: {人間関係|にんげんかんけい}が{煩|わずら}わしいと{感|かん}じることがある。
examples.english: Sometimes I find interpersonal relationships bothersome.

examples.japanese: {煩|わずら}わしい{質問|しつもん}には{答|こた}えたくない。
examples.english: I don't want to answer annoying questions.

notes:
FORMS:
・Adverbial: {煩|わずら}わしく
・Noun form: {煩|わずら}わしさ

{煩|わずら}わしい describes things that are complicated, require effort, or cause mental burden. Often used for:
・Administrative procedures
・Social obligations
・Complicated relationships

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{手続|てつづ}きが{煩|わずら}わしい (procedures are troublesome)
・{煩|わずら}わしいことを{避|さ}ける (avoid troublesome things)

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{面倒|めんどう}: General trouble or bother
・{煩|わずら}わしい: More formal, emphasizes mental burden
・{鬱陶|うっとう}しい: Gloomy/oppressive annoyance

REGISTER: Slightly formal; used in both written and spoken Japanese.
